Chief_Complaint.content: Patient presents with a strange, non-painful swelling on his left elbow, noticed about a week ago.
Chief_Complaint.source_text: have like a weird swelling on, on, on my elbow... It's not painful at all

History_of_Present_Illness.content: The swelling on the left elbow feels slightly warm and contains fluid.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: it's slightly warm... I, I, cannot feel like this, little bit fluid in inside

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient denies any recent trauma or injury to the elbow and has normal range of motion.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: have you banged that elbow? Do you have any kind of injury? No, not really... I can actually like move it normally.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: This is the first time this has happened.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: has this happened before? No, no I haven't noticed that before.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient works a desk job and is not physically active at work.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: do you do anything physical? Not really. No, I just, you know sit at a desk.

Past_Medical_History.content: Patient was diagnosed with osteoarthritis by a GP a few years ago.
Past_Medical_History.source_text: I think I have something like uh, osteoarthritis... Has anyone ever told you that? Um, yes. Yes, a few years ago... a a GP.

Past_Medical_History.content: Patient has no other significant past medical history.
Past_Medical_History.source_text: do you have any other illnesses at all? Well not, not really, no.

Medications.source_text: are you on any medication on a regular basis? Uh, no.

Adverse_Drug_Reactions_and_Allergies.content: Patient is allergic to peanuts but has no known medication allergies.
Adverse_Drug_Reactions_and_Allergies.source_text: I'm, I'm allergic to, to peanuts... are, are you allergic to any medication? Uh, no. Not that I know of.

Family_History.content: Patient reports no family history of rheumatological diseases.
Family_History.source_text: Has anyone in your family, got any, kind of rheumatology, diseases... Um, no... in my family, I'm not sure.

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient is John Smith, 53 years old.
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: my name is John Smith... I'm uh, fifty three.

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient is physically active, running 2-3 times per week.
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: I do, I do some sports. I run regularly, like two, three times a week.

Assessment.content: The impression is possible olecranon bursitis of the left elbow.
Assessment.source_text: this seems like uh, what we call the Bursitis. OK. So, that's an inflammation of one of the fluid sacs around the joint.

Plan_of_Care.content: Recommended taking regular anti-inflammatory medication: Ibuprofen 400mg twice a day, after food.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: I, I would take Ibuprofen regularly, OK... that's four hundred milligrams, two times a day. And you should take, take that after food

Plan_of_Care.content: Arrange rheumatology blood tests (ESR, CRP, FBC, Rheumatoid Factor, Urate) to investigate other causes of joint swelling.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: get some blood tests done, to check for other types of uh, causes of joint swelling... having some tests done to check for inflammatory markers, infection, rheumatological antibodies... also check for things like Gout as well

Follow_up_Information.content: Patient will be sent blood test forms and should contact the practice to arrange a follow-up review (video or in-person) after the tests are done.
Follow_up_Information.source_text: we're going to arrange some, um, blood test forms to be sent out to your house... you contact us, , after you've had the blood test done, and we can review things then, OK.

Follow_up_Information.content: Advised on red flag symptoms of septic arthritis (worsening redness, pain, or spreading erythema) and to seek urgent review if these occur.
Follow_up_Information.source_text: if your, the elbow was to become very red, very painful, uh, and the redness was to spread or become uh, you know more intense. Then you need to get on the phone or get, have a video appointment , with one of us as soon as possible.
